या देवी सर्वभूतेषु is one of 24 verses in Devī Māhātmya chapter 5, numbered Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa 85.12–85.35 in the GRETIL e-text; the mother verse is 85.34.

faqs.question: How do you say Happy Navratri in Sanskrit?
faqs.answer: The dictionary form of the festival is the neuter noun नवरात्र, so the simplest correct greeting is शुभं नवरात्रम् (śubhaṃ navarātram), "a blessed Navarātra". If you use the form नवरात्रि and treat it as feminine like रात्रि, say शुभा नवरात्रिः (śubhā navarātriḥ) instead.

faqs.question: Is "Ya Devi Sarvabhuteshu" from the Durga Saptashati?
faqs.answer: Yes. It is the refrain of a hymn in chapter 5 of the Devī Māhātmya, which the GRETIL e-text numbers as Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa 85.12 to 85.35: 24 verses, each naming one form in which the Goddess dwells in all beings. The power verse is 85.18 and the mother verse is 85.34.

faqs.question: What does Sarva Mangala Mangalye mean in English?
faqs.answer: It addresses the Goddess as "the auspiciousness of all that is auspicious", then calls her kind, the fulfiller of every aim, the refuge, three-eyed Gaurī and Nārāyaṇī, and ends with "salutation to you". It is Devī Māhātmya chapter 11, numbered Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa 91.9 in the GRETIL edition.

faqs.question: Which Sanskrit shlok can I send my mother for Navratri?
faqs.answer: Send या देवी सर्वभूतेषु मातृरूपेण संस्थिता, "the Goddess who dwells in all beings as mother", Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa 85.34. Check that your copy reads मातृरूपेण; a circulating version replaces it with the Hindi word माँ.

faqs.question: What is a short Navratri status in Sanskrit?
faqs.answer: For a composed line, नव रात्रयः, नवाशिषः (nava rātrayaḥ, navāśiṣaḥ), "nine nights, nine blessings", is four words. For scripture, the first half of या देवी सर्वभूतेषु शक्तिरूपेण संस्थिता fits a status and can be credited to Devī Māhātmya chapter 5.

faqs.question: Why do Durga Saptashati verse numbers differ from book to book?
faqs.answer: The GRETIL e-text numbers the 13 chapters (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa 81 to 93) as 588 verses, while recitation editions count the same text to 700, which is where the name Saptaśatī comes from. Quote the chapter as well as the verse, and say which edition you used.

faqs.question: Is "Dehi Saubhagyam Arogyam" part of the Devi Mahatmya?
faqs.answer: No. It is verse 12 of the Argalā Stotra, a hymn recited before the 13 chapters, not one of them. The edition on sanskritdocuments.org reads देहि सौभाग्यमारोग्यं देहि देवि परं सुखम्, not "देहि मे परमं सुखम्".

faqs.question: Should I say the h at the end of namah?
faqs.answer: Lightly. The ḥ in IAST is visarga, a soft breath that echoes the vowel before it, so नमः ends close to "namaha" with a faint final a. The long vowels ā, ī and ū matter more: hold them twice as long as the short ones.

faqs.question: Are the composed Sanskrit greetings on this page real shlokas?
faqs.answer: No. The eight composed lines were written for this page in 2026 and checked against Monier-Williams; they are modern Sanskrit, not scripture. Forward them as greetings, and keep the label "shlok" for the five sourced verses.

faqs.question: Can I put Sanskrit lines on the Be My Dandiya Partner page?
faqs.answer: The page takes nine short lines, one for each night, and you can type your own text into them, but its interface is in English. Preview the page after typing Devanagari so you can see how it displays before you publish and send the link.

faqs.question: When should I send Navratri shubhkamnayein in Sanskrit?
faqs.answer: Sharad Navratri begins on 11 October in 2026 and 30 September in 2027 (Drik Panchang, New Delhi). In SubhSandesh's Raksha Bandhan 2026 sample of 89 pages, 49.4% were built on the festival day itself, which suggests sending on the first night rather than days ahead.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Navratri Wishes in Sanskrit, With Verse Numbers and Meanings

The most reliable Navratri wishes in Sanskrit are verses quoted exactly from the Devī Māhātmya, such as सर्वमङ्गलमाङ्गल्ये शिवे सर्वार्थसाधिके (chapter 11), or short greetings built on the dictionary form of the festival's name, such as शुभं नवरात्रम् (śubhaṃ navarātram, "a blessed Navarātra"). Every line is labelled as scripture, with chapter and verse checked against a digital edition, or as a modern greeting we composed.

Two SubhSandesh measurements shaped the format. 48.3% of shared pages are opened on a phone, so each verse is cut to two lines with IAST beneath it, and in our Raksha Bandhan 2026 sample (n = 89 pages, a different festival used as the nearest analogue) 49.4% of pages were built on the festival day itself. Below: grammar, five sourced verses, the nine forms, eight composed greetings and pronunciation.

## Is it नवरात्रि or नवरात्र in Sanskrit?

Classical Sanskrit calls the festival नवरात्र (navarātra), a neuter noun. [Monier-Williams' Sanskrit-English Dictionary, page 531](https://sanskrit-lexicon.uni-koeln.de/scans/csl-apidev/getword.php?dict=mw&key=navarAtra&input=slp1&output=deva) defines it as "the 9 days from the 1st of the light half of month Āśvina to the 9th (devoted to the worship of Durgā)", and has no headword navarātri. Apte and the Shabda-Sagara, on the same server, agree.

So the adjective is neuter: शुभं नवरात्रम्; "of Navarātra" is नवरात्रस्य. If you prefer नवरात्रि and treat it like feminine रात्रि (night), the adjective turns feminine: शुभा नवरात्रिः (śubhā navarātriḥ).

Avoid शुभ नवरात्रिः, which a widely copied wishes page prints: a bare stem with a gap before the noun. Joined as one compound, शुभनवरात्रिः, it is acceptable.

## 5 Sanskrit verses for Navratri wishes, with chapter and verse

The Devī Māhātmya is chapters 81 to 93 of the Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, which the [GRETIL e-text (SUB Göttingen, version of 31 July 2020)](https://gretil.sub.uni-goettingen.de/gretil/corpustei/transformations/plaintext/sa_mArkaNDeyapurANa1-93.txt) numbers as 588 verses. Editions sold as the Durgā Saptaśatī ("the seven hundred") count it to 700, so verse numbers differ between books.

References give the Purāṇa number (MkP), then the Devī Māhātmya chapter (DM). GRETIL warns its text "is not proof-read"; one typo is corrected below.

### 1. Yā devī… śaktirūpeṇa: the Goddess as power (MkP 85.18, DM 5)

- **Sanskrit:** या देवी सर्वभूतेषु शक्तिरूपेण संस्थिता । नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमो नमः ॥
- **IAST:** yā devī sarvabhūteṣu śaktirūpeṇa saṃsthitā / namastasyai namastasyai namastasyai namo namaḥ
- **Meaning:** "To the Goddess who dwells in all beings as power: salutation to her, again and again."
- **Suits:** anyone. It is one of 24 "yā devī" verses in this hymn (MkP 85.12 to 85.35).

### 2. Yā devī… mātṛrūpeṇa: the Goddess as mother (MkP 85.34, DM 5)

- **Sanskrit:** या देवी सर्वभूतेषु मातृरूपेण संस्थिता । नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमो नमः ॥
- **IAST:** yā devī sarvabhūteṣu mātṛrūpeṇa saṃsthitā / namastasyai namastasyai namastasyai namo namaḥ
- **Meaning:** "To the Goddess who dwells in all beings as mother: salutation to her, again and again."
- **Suits:** your mother. A circulating version slips in the Hindi माँ (सर्वभूतानां माँ स्वरूपेण); the edition has मातृरूपेण.

### 3. Sarvamaṅgalamāṅgalye: the family verse (MkP 91.9, DM 11)

- **Sanskrit:** सर्वमङ्गलमाङ्गल्ये शिवे सर्वार्थसाधिके । शरण्ये त्र्यम्बके गौरि नारायणि नमोऽस्तु ते ॥
- **IAST:** sarvamaṅgalamāṅgalye śive sarvārthasādhike / śaraṇye tryambake gauri nārāyaṇi namo 'stu te
- **Meaning:** "Auspiciousness of all that is auspicious, kind one, fulfiller of every aim, refuge, three-eyed Gaurī, Nārāyaṇī: salutation to you."
- **Suits:** parents and family groups. The IAST apostrophe marks the avagraha ऽ, an elided "a".

### 4. Śaratkāle mahāpūjā: the verse that names autumn worship (MkP 92.11–12, DM 12)

- **Sanskrit:** शरत्काले महापूजा क्रियते या च वार्षिकी । तस्यां ममैतन्माहात्म्यं श्रुत्वा भक्तिसमन्वितः ॥ सर्वबाधाविनिर्मुक्तो धनधान्यसमन्वितः । मनुष्यो मत्प्रसादेन भविष्यति न संशयः ॥
- **IAST:** śaratkāle mahāpūjā kriyate yā ca vārṣikī / tasyāṃ mamaitanmāhātmyaṃ śrutvā bhaktisamanvitaḥ // sarvabādhāvinirmukto dhanadhānyasamanvitaḥ / manuṣyo matprasādena bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
- **Meaning:** the Goddess speaks: "Whoever devoutly hears my glorification at the great annual autumn worship will, by my grace, be freed from every obstacle and blessed with wealth and grain, without doubt."
- **Suits:** a long family message; it is the one verse that names the autumn festival. GRETIL types vinirmṛkto, corrected to vinirmukto.

### 5. Dehi saubhāgyam ārogyam: a health wish (Argalā Stotra, verse 12)

- **Sanskrit:** देहि सौभाग्यमारोग्यं देहि देवि परं सुखम् ।
- **IAST:** dehi saubhāgyam ārogyaṃ dehi devi paraṃ sukham
- **Meaning:** "Grant good fortune and health, O Devī; grant the highest happiness."
- **Suits:** grandparents. It sits outside the 13 chapters, in the [Argalā Stotra on sanskritdocuments.org](https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/argalaastotra.html), recited before them. Send this half only; the second ends द्विषो जहि, "destroy the hostile". The popular "देहि मे परमं सुखम्" is not the edition's text.

## The nine forms of Durga in Sanskrit, night by night

The nine names come from verses 3 to 5 of the [Devī Kavaca on sanskritdocuments.org](https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/dkavach.html): प्रथमं शैलपुत्री च द्वितीयं ब्रह्मचारिणी (prathamaṃ śailaputrī ca dvitīyaṃ brahmacāriṇī). Like the Argalā, it is recited "as a limb of the Saptaśatī" (सप्तशती पाठाङ्गत्वेन); a [2019 Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies lecture by Silje Lyngar Einarsen](https://ochs.org.uk/lecture/text-paratext-and-practice-of-the-devimahatmya-mt19/) argues such "paratextual elements" shape how the text is received.

The lines below are half-verses from a [Navadurgā Stotra on sanskritdocuments.org](https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_devii/navadurga.html), which names no older source. They go by night, not date: in 2026 Saptamī spans 17 and 18 October.

- **Night 1, Śailaputrī:** वृषारूढां शूलधरां शैलपुत्रीं यशस्विनीम् (*vṛṣārūḍhāṃ śūladharāṃ śailaputrīṃ yaśasvinīm*): "I bow to glorious Śailaputrī, riding a bull, holding a trident."
- **Night 2, Brahmacāriṇī:** देवी प्रसीदतु मयि ब्रह्मचारिण्यनुत्तमा (*devī prasīdatu mayi brahmacāriṇy anuttamā*): "May the peerless Devī Brahmacāriṇī be gracious to me."
- **Night 3, Candraghaṇṭā:** प्रसादं तनुते मह्यं चन्द्रघण्टेति विश्रुता (*prasādaṃ tanute mahyaṃ candraghaṇṭeti viśrutā*): "Renowned as Candraghaṇṭā, she extends her grace to me."
- **Night 4, Kūṣmāṇḍā:** दधाना हस्तपद्माभ्यां कूष्माण्डा शुभदास्तु मे (*dadhānā hastapadmābhyāṃ kūṣmāṇḍā śubhadāstu me*): "Holding two pots in her lotus hands, may Kūṣmāṇḍā bring me good."
- **Night 5, Skandamātā:** शुभदास्तु सदा देवी स्कन्दमाता यशस्विनी (*śubhadāstu sadā devī skandamātā yaśasvinī*): "May glorious Skandamātā always bring good."
- **Night 6, Kātyāyanī:** कात्यायनी शुभं दद्याद्देवी दानवघातिनी (*kātyāyanī śubhaṃ dadyād devī dānavaghātinī*): "May Kātyāyanī, slayer of demons, grant good."
- **Night 7, Kālarātri:** जय सर्वगते देवि कालरात्रि नमोऽस्तु ते (*jaya sarvagate devi kālarātri namo 'stu te*): "Victory, all-pervading Devī; Kālarātri, salutation to you." (Argalā, verse 1)
- **Night 8, Mahāgaurī:** महागौरी शुभं दद्यान्महादेवप्रमोददा (*mahāgaurī śubhaṃ dadyān mahādevapramodadā*): "May Mahāgaurī, who delights Mahādeva, grant good."
- **Night 9, Siddhidātrī:** सेव्यमाना सदा भूयात् सिद्धिदा सिद्धिदायिनी (*sevyamānā sadā bhūyāt siddhidā siddhidāyinī*): "Ever worshipped, may she be the giver of attainment."

The stotra's Kālarātri verse describes a terrifying form with no blessing, so night 7 borrows the Argalā's opening. The edition's दद्यादेवी is corrected to दद्याद्देवी (dadyāt + devī).

## 8 composed Sanskrit greetings and status lines (modern, not scripture)

These are ours, composed in 2026 and checked against Monier-Williams. Do not forward them as shlokas. Sandhi is the commonest slip: प्रसादः भवतु becomes प्रसादो भवतु.

- शुभं नवरात्रम्। (*śubhaṃ navarātram*): "A blessed Navarātra."
- नवरात्रस्य शुभाशिषः। (*navarātrasya śubhāśiṣaḥ*): "Good wishes for Navarātra." (शुभाशिस्, "good wishes", Monier-Williams page 1083)
- भवते नवरात्रस्य शुभकामनाः। (*bhavate navarātrasya śubhakāmanāḥ*): "Navarātra wishes to you." Use भवत्यै (bhavatyai) for a woman.
- दुर्गा त्वां पातु। (*durgā tvāṃ pātu*): "May Durgā protect you." Informal.
- अस्माकं कुलं माता दुर्गा रक्षतु। (*asmākaṃ kulaṃ mātā durgā rakṣatu*): "May Mother Durgā protect our family."
- प्रतिरात्रं ते देव्याः प्रसादो भवतु। (*pratirātraṃ te devyāḥ prasādo bhavatu*): "May the Goddess's grace be with you every night."
- नव रात्रयः, नवाशिषः। (*nava rātrayaḥ, navāśiṣaḥ*): "Nine nights, nine blessings."
- जय दुर्गे। (*jaya durge*): "Victory, O Durgā."

## How to read the IAST: 8 marks that change the sound

IAST (International Alphabet of Sanskrit Transliteration) writes each Devanagari letter one way only. Eight marks matter most:

- **ā ī ū:** held twice as long; śubhā is not śubha.
- **ṛ:** a vowel, said "ri", so mātṛ sounds like "maatri".
- **ṃ:** a nasal, coloured by the next consonant.
- **ḥ:** visarga, a breath echoing the vowel: namaḥ ends near "namaha".
- **ś, ṣ:** both "sh"; ṣ with the tongue curled back.
- **ṅ:** the "ng" of "sing", as in maṅgala.
- **ṭ ḍ ṇ:** retroflex, tongue curled back, unlike t d n.
- **c:** always "ch": candraghaṇṭā is "chandraghanta".

## Scripture or composed: which Sanskrit line fits which message

The table compares each kind of line by source, length and use.

| Line | Type and source | Words | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|
| या देवी… शक्तिरूपेण | Scripture, DM 5, MkP 85.18 | 10 | Status, any recipient |
| सर्वमङ्गलमाङ्गल्ये… | Scripture, DM 11, MkP 91.9 | 9 | Parents, family group |
| शरत्काले महापूजा… | Scripture, DM 12, MkP 92.11–12 | 17 | Long message |
| Navadurgā half-line | Stotra, sanskritdocuments.org | 4 to 6 | One line per night |
| शुभं नवरात्रम् | Composed, 2026 | 2 | Quick reply |

Copy scripture exactly; edit composed lines only if you can check the grammar.

## When to send, and when one page beats a forward

Sharad Navratri runs 11 to 19 October 2026 and 30 September to 8 October 2027 (Drik Panchang, New Delhi). Our only festival timing data is Raksha Bandhan 2026: of 89 pages, 49.4% were built on the day and 27.0% the day before. No Navratri data exists yet, but that points to the first night.

If the wish is really an invitation for one person, a forwarded verse cannot carry it. The [Be My Dandiya Partner page](https://subhsandesh.in/dandiya-partner) takes nine short lines, one per night, shown as the recipient lights nine diyas round a garbo, so the half-lines above fit one per diya. Its interface is English; preview your Devanagari before you publish.

It is a one-to-one invitation for your love, your crush or a best friend as garba buddy, not a group wish. You can add a password at publish, as 38.5% of SubhSandesh creators do. If the message is "I love you" more than "come to garba", the [romantic I love you page](https://subhsandesh.in/love-gf) says it better.

## Where Sanskrit wishes go wrong, and where SubhSandesh loses

Most errors are ordinary: Hindi inside a verse (माँ for मातृ), a missing case ending, or a mantra with no source. We left out bīja mantras because none of the four texts checked offers one as a greeting.

SubhSandesh is the wrong choice in three cases. A grandparent who reads Sanskrit on paper deserves a handwritten card with verse 91.9. A society group needs one forwarded line, not a personal page, and nothing on our pages checks your Sanskrit.

## Sources

- Mārkaṇḍeyapurāṇa 1–93, GRETIL e-text, version of 31 July 2020.
- Monier-Williams, Sanskrit-English Dictionary (1899), pages 531 and 1083.
- Argalā Stotra, Devī Kavaca (updated 1 May 2020), Navadurgā Stotra: sanskritdocuments.org.
- Einarsen, OCHS lecture, 7 November 2019.

auditReport.honestAssessment: An answer engine has a concrete reason to cite this over the five pages analysed: it is the only one that gives verse references checked against an edition, separates scripture from composed lines, explains the नवरात्र/नवरात्रि grammar, and flags three misquotations the incumbents print. It cannot overcome the domain-authority gap, the first-party facts are platform-wide rather than about Sanskrit, and no peer-reviewed paper on the Devī Māhātmya could be read open-access this run.

structuralLimitations: Prompt suggested शुभा नवरात्रिः as a model greeting. Monier-Williams, Apte, Shabda-Sagara and PWG all list only navarātra (neuter for the festival); none has navarātri. शुभा नवरात्रिः is grammatical only if नवरात्रि is treated as feminine like रात्रि. The post gives शुभं नवरात्रम् as the dictionary-safe form and explains both.

Prompt allowed the nine forms' dhyana lines 'ONLY if you can source each'. They are not in the Devī Māhātmya (absent from GRETIL MkP 81–93): the names come from the Devī Kavaca vv. 3–5 and the dhyāna verses from a Navadurgā Stotra on sanskritdocuments.org that names no older source. Each is labelled as such; Kālarātri's stotra verse carries no blessing, so night 7 uses Argalā verse 1 instead, disclosed in the body.

No peer-reviewed open-access paper read. Padoux 1993 (Persée, OA) returned 403 to the fetcher; Einarsen 2018 and Simmons 2025 SUNY chapters are closed (Unpaywall/OpenAlex). The scholarly sources are the GRETIL edition (SUB Göttingen) and an OCHS lecture abstract. OpenAlex search was rate-limited.
